title: Deterministic Offline Rendering & Snapshot Pipeline Architecture

blocks.content: Engineering notebook from `docs/OFFLINE_RENDER_MANAGER_AND_SNAPSHOT_ARCHITECTURE.md`. This archive preserves the project’s original rationale, equations, performance reports and illustrative code. Historical paths, API names, claims and sketches can differ from the current engine. For copy-ready programs use the guides and demos; for current callable signatures use the source-derived API. Performance figures here describe reported experiments, not guaranteed frame rates.

blocks.text: Original document: [docs/OFFLINE_RENDER_MANAGER_AND_SNAPSHOT_ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/docs/OFFLINE_RENDER_MANAGER_AND_SNAPSHOT_ARCHITECTURE.md). See [current limitations](/limitations) for concrete compatibility notes.
Exporting broadcast-quality 4K 60 FPS videos and high-resolution mathematical publication snapshots requires a rendering pipeline independent of wall-clock hardware limitations.
Retiam provides three distinct capture systems:

items: **[`OfflineRenderManager`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/OfflineRenderManager.ts)**: Deterministic frame-by-frame stepping engine that freezes real-time playback, advances time by exact discrete intervals ($\Delta t = 1 / \text{FPS}$), reads back GPU framebuffers with 256-byte alignment, and streams raw frames to an external encoder.
**[`SnapshotManager`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/SnapshotManager.ts)**: Single-frame high-resolution image capture engine (PNG, WebP, JPEG).

**[`OfflineRecorder`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/recorder/OfflineRecorder.ts) & [`Recorder`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/recorder/Recorder.ts)**: Headless WebSocket client streaming raw audio and RGBA/float pixels to the local Node.js FFmpeg CLI process, alongside client-side WebCodecs canvas recording with [`Recorder`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/recorder/Recorder.ts).

blocks.text: Real-time rendering relies on `requestAnimationFrame`, where variable CPU/GPU load produces dropped frames and variable $\Delta t$. During offline rendering, Retiam disables wall-clock execution:

items: **Discrete Clock Stepping**: Time advances strictly by $1 / F$ seconds per step:

**Synchronous Asset Decoding**: Video entities ([`RTVideo`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/3d/RTVideo.ts)) seek to $t_{k+1}$ and await the HTML5 `seeked` event before the frame renders.
**Asynchronous Readback Lock**: The simulation halts execution until the GPU signals that the current frame's pixel memory has been transferred into system RAM.

blocks.text: WebGPU requires texture buffer copy operations to satisfy strict memory layout constraints:

items: **Row Pitch Alignment**: Every row of pixels written to a `GPUBuffer` must be a multiple of **256 bytes**:

blocks.text: The `SnapshotManager` captures high-resolution stills for research publications and video thumbnails:

items: **Offscreen Resolution Scaling**: Can render frames at arbitrary target resolutions (e.g. $7680 \times 4320$ 8K) independently of the physical display monitor.

blocks.text: The offline render architecture powers all CLI commands documented in [`CLI_COMMANDS_AND_TOOLING_REFERENCE.md`](/notes-cli-commands-and-tooling-reference):

items: **`retiam render <scene> --output video.mp4 --res 4k --fps 60`**: Spawns a headless Puppeteer/Chrome browser instance with `--enable-unsafe-webgpu`, attaches `OfflineRenderManager`, and pipes frames into `ffmpeg`.
**`retiam snapshot <scene> -t 5.2 -o thumbnail.png`**: Fast-forwards to time $t=5.2\text{s}$, captures a single frame via `SnapshotManager`, and exits.
